why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief. Step 6 of the builder brief ("Self-check before opening the PR") copies the verifier's probes word for word. `test "$(node bin/greet.js --shout Ada)" = "HELLO, ADA!" && echo PASS || echo FAIL` is the same as Check 1, `test "$(node bin/greet.js Ada)" = "Hello, Ada!" && echo PASS || echo FAIL` is the same as Check 2, and `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` is the same as Check 3. These are inline scripts with expected outputs, PASS/FAIL conditions and a grep, not just a command named by an expect line or the repository's tests. Telling the builder to run `npm test` is allowed, but sharing these probes breaks the rule that the builder brief carries none of the verifier's checks.
